newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Grintek shares jump ahead of announcement.
newsitem.headline: Grintek shares jump ahead of announcement.

text.p: News of a significant announcement later on Thursday triggered a jump in shares of South African electronics groups Grintek Ltd and Siltek Ltd, adding to the recent interest in local information technology stocks.
Dealers said the market was reacting positively once again to the possibility of a restructuring in the information technology sector.
"We're heading for a total restructure there and this is good news," one dealer said.

Grintek jumped to a day's high of 410 cents from its previous close of 390 cents shortly after news of the pending announcement. By 0925 GMT it had retreated slightly to 405 cents amid a volume of 54,500 shares.
Siltek rose 50 cents to 23.50 rand in volume of 16,400 shares.
Grintek said earlier it would give details at a press conference at 5.00 p.m. (1500 GMT) about an important deal likely to affect it, Siltek and the entire information technology sector.

"Grintek Ltd has decided to hold a press conference and give details of a significant move which will affect Grintek and Siltek and impact on the South African information technology scene as a whole," it said.
Analysts speculated as to what the move would entail.

"The possible scenarios are either to unbundle Grintek and give shareholders a direct interest in Siltek and Grinaker Electronics, or list Grinaker Electronics as a separate company," said SocGen Frankel Pollak analyst Ricahrd Muller.
Listing Grinaker Electronics as a separate company would unlock its true value, he said.
Grintek has a 92.5 percent stake in Grinaker Electronics.
Shares in another information technology firm, Persetel Holdings sparked up on Tuesday, driven by market speculation it was poised to take a controlling stake in Q Data Ltd.

Persetel and Q Data enjoyed more interest on Thursday following the Grintek announcement. Persetel was last 25 cents up at 27 rand in a traded volume of 180,500 shares, while Q Data rose to a day's high of 922 cents from its previous close of 906 cents, before losing a little to 920 cents.
Analysts and dealers said interest in Persetel could be linked to moves in Siltek.
"Persetel could by into Q Data via the Siltek shareholding," Muller said.
Grintek holds 56.9 percent of Siltek, which holds 44.1 percent of Q Data.
